config_name: Steam Deck OLED — Custom AMD 'Sephiroth' Zen 2 8-core / 8 RDNA2 CUs, 16GB LPDDR5-6400, 1TB NVMe, 7.4" 1280x800 90Hz HDR OLED anti-glare etched glass

specs.display_type: HDR OLED, 10-bit, P3 wide gamut, touch, anti-glare etched glass
specs.ports: 1x USB-C 3.1 Gen1 (DP alt-mode, PD), microSD UHS-I, 3.5mm
specs.keyboard_notes: no keyboard; on-screen keyboard in SteamOS/Desktop mode
specs.os: SteamOS 3 (Arch Linux + KDE Plasma desktop mode)

battery.notes: 50Wh, identical to 512GB OLED. Engadget measured Hades 4h23m, Elden Ring maxed 2h20m on the same hardware.

price.notes: LIST.md estimate (C$200 premium over verified C$1,349 512GB, matching US$549/$649 gap); 1TB listed on steamdeck.com but CAD price not shown.

offers.name: Steam Deck OLED 7” 90Hz HDR Touchscreen Handheld Gaming PC (AMD Zen 2/AMD RDNA 3/16GB RAM/1TB SSD/SteamOS)

reviews.quote: the premium $649 edition packs a big 1TB SSD and an anti-reflective display... The Steam Deck OLED impresses thanks to its vibrant display, lighter design, faster Wi-Fi and improved cooling.
This isn't the Steam Deck 2 some are waiting for, it's just a welcome improvement on an already good device.

praises: Etched anti-glare glass diffuses outdoor/light reflections far better than the glossy 512GB — big win for window-side couch gaming
1TB means AAA installs (Cyberpunk ~160GB) plus a retro emulation library without juggling the slow microSD slot
Same OLED HDR 90Hz panel as the 512GB — pure blacks and 1000-nit HDR highlights
SSD is a standard M.2 2230 anyway, so buyers who'd have upgraded the 512GB see the C$200 premium as fair
SteamOS console-like sleep/resume and Valve's first-party replacement parts keep long-term ownership easy
complaints: Etched glass adds a faint sparkle/grain to fine text and desktop mode that some users dislike after the glossy OLED
Identical 2021-era APU to every other Deck — C$1,549 in 2026 buys faster Xbox Ally X or Legion Go 2
Bulkiest-in-class 640g+ footprint; anti-glare doesn't help the small-hands ergonomics
Anti-cheat multiplayer games remain unplayable on SteamOS regardless of storage tier
1TB OLED has periodically been the hardest SKU to get stock of at Canadian retail

design_philosophy: The top of Valve's current OLED lineup: identical hardware to the reviewed 512GB with double the storage and the signature etched anti-glare glass, aimed at users who install many AAA titles and play in bright rooms. It keeps Valve's console-like, repair-friendly formula unchanged.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from the OLED 512GB anchor (SHARED-steam-deck.md): identical internals; deltas are +1.0 readability_bright for etched anti-glare glass, −0.1 screen_quality for slight etch sparkle, +0.5 storage headroom (no rating change needed). Price estimated per LIST.md.
